contradictions.detail: The dealer text says 'clean car-fax' and the Autotrader widget says 'No Accident or Damage Reported'. The attached CARFAX reports minor damage on 08/06/2025.

The listing sells the car as an Autobahn. The attached CARFAX decodes this VIN as a GTI SE. The difference affects value, and on the DCC/ACC equipment it determines whether the listed features are actually present.
The Autotrader history widget says 'Single Owner'. The dealer text ('two owner') and the CARFAX (2 owners) agree on two.
The description quotes 228 hp, a 2018+ Performance Pack figure. A 2017 GTI was rated 210 hp, or 220 hp with the Performance Pack.

critical_evidence.evidence: There is no statement and no scan data on ECU software. The VW dealer service visit in 08/2025 is weakly reassuring but not proof. The black badges are cosmetic only. A tune check is needed: ECU part/software number against stock, plus a CA smog-readiness scan.

CARFAX line 08/08/2025, 34,544 mi, Safford Volkswagen West: 'Thermostat housing/gasket replaced; Thermostat replaced' (the EA888 Gen3 pump/thermostat housing area). No invoice attached to show the exact parts.

documentation.rationale: Both halves are partly present. Identity and terms are solid: VIN, itemised $18,999 + $385 doc fee, a guaranteed-clean title and a 2-owner CARFAX. Maintenance evidence comes through the CARFAX: dated thermostat-housing and brake-fluid service 08/2025, plus dealer and independent visits. Gaps remain: no invoices, the trim is disputed, only one oil change is reported, and nothing documents the 2025 damage repair or the tune status.

condition.rationale: The photos show straight panels, a clean front end and stock ride height. Cooling and brake-fluid work is documented. Against that, minor damage was reported 08/2025 and apparent scuffing near the right-rear fuel door is visible. Tire age is unknown, and the last reported replacement was 2020. There is no PPI, no underside photos and no interior photos here.

price_value.rationale: $19,384 all-in from the dealer for a 39k-mile manual 2017 sits within the market band. Autotrader puts it ~$976 below its estimate, and a 2019 Autobahn at 57k sold for $22,000. The price assumes Autobahn spec, which the CARFAX decode disputes, and a 'clean' Carfax, which is not accurate. The likely tire replacement also counts against value.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual, priced inside the ideal band, practical, and serviceable by Jason's VW mechanic. A hatchback with a sunroof is fine year-round once the drains are checked. However, the GTI is his lukewarm fallback, not the RF or Z3 target.

logistics.rationale: Retail dealer in Louisville, KY, about 1,900 miles away. A mobile PPI on the lot is likely arrangeable but not confirmed. It would be a fly-out and drive-home purchase. CA registration and smog look feasible for a stock car.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Gray over black with a 6-speed is a desirable combination. If it really is an Autobahn with the Performance Pack (LSD, red calipers), that is a genuine plus, but it is unconfirmed. The aftermarket black badges are cosmetic, and Jason is lukewarm on the model.

seller_questions: The CARFAX you supplied shows minor damage on 08/06/2025. Which panel was damaged, who repaired it, and can you send the repair invoice or photos?
Can you send a photo of the window sticker, or a VW build-data printout for VIN [VIN], confirming Autobahn vs SE and whether it has the Performance Pack?
Can you send close-up photos of the right-rear quarter panel around the fuel door and of all four bumper corners in good light?
What are the DOT date codes on all four tires, and what is the tread depth?
Can you send a full OBD/VCDS scan, including ECU software part number and readiness monitors, to confirm stock software?
Did the car come with any service records or receipts from the previous owner beyond the CARFAX, especially oil changes since 2021?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, showing the dash with no warning lights and the idle for 60 seconds?
Will you allow an independent mobile inspector to do a PPI on your lot, with a lift if available, before any deposit?
Were the black VW emblems added by you or by the prior owner, and are there any other modifications (intake, exhaust, downpipe, diverter valve)?
Does the clutch slip in 4th–5th under full throttle at low rpm, and has it ever been replaced?
Can you send interior photos: seats, headliner around the sunroof, and the footwells and spare-tire well for water?
ppi_focus: Paint-meter all panels, especially the right-rear quarter and rear bumper, to locate the 08/2025 damage and judge the repair quality
Confirm trim and options: DCC drive modes working, ACC radar present, navigation, front LSD/Performance Pack (caliper logo, VAG build codes)
Read ECU software ID and adaptation history for a current or removed tune, and check emissions readiness monitors for CA smog
Clutch slip test under load in high gear, clutch engagement point, and dual-mass flywheel rattle at idle
Water pump / thermostat housing area: confirm the 2025 part is dry and the coolant level is stable after a heat cycle
Sunroof drains and seals, plus carpet and spare-well dampness, for the year-round rain use
Tire DOT codes and tread, plus inner-edge wear indicating alignment issues
Underside for scrapes on the front lip and subframe, and oil leaks at the PCV/valve cover and rear main
Full module scan for stored faults (the instrument cluster and radio were replaced in 2019)
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a repair invoice or paint-meter result showing the 08/2025 damage was cosmetic and properly fixed
Up: a window sticker or build data confirming Autobahn with the Performance Pack, plus a stock-ECU scan
Up: tires under ~6 years old and a clean independent PPI with no clutch slip
Down: evidence of panel replacement or structural repair, a current or removed tune, or a slipping clutch
Down: the dealer refusing an independent PPI or declining to explain the damage report
evidence.mission_note: A manual, well-priced, practical GTI fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and suits Jason's VW-friendly mechanic. It remains his lukewarm fallback rather than the MX-5 RF or Z3 he actually wants, so it ranks mainly as a pragmatic bridge.
evidence.rationale: The attached CARFAX establishes two personal owners, a guaranteed-clean title, and mileage consistent with the listing (38,317 in 06/2026 vs 39,340 now). It also documents key age-related work: a VW-dealer thermostat housing and thermostat replacement plus a brake-fluid flush in 08/2025. The same report contradicts the dealer's 'clean car-fax' with a minor-damage report dated 08/06/2025 for which no repair record exists. A side photo shows what appears to be scuffing near the right-rear fuel door. The trim is disputed: the listing says Autobahn, the CARFAX decodes SE. That leaves the DCC, ACC, navigation and LSD claims unconfirmed and affects how the $19,384 all-in price compares with the 2019 Autobahn comp at $22,000. Still open are ECU tune status and CA smog readiness, tire age (last reported replacement 05/2020), clutch condition, oil-change history after 2021, and whether a mobile PPI can happen on the lot before money moves.
evidence.next_action: Email Epic Automotive asking for the 08/2025 damage details and repair documentation, the window sticker or VW build data for this VIN, tire DOT codes, and written agreement to an independent mobile PPI with a tune/readiness scan before any deposit.
